newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Talks with Khmer Rouge illegal - Cambodian PM.
newsitem.headline: Talks with Khmer Rouge illegal - Cambodian PM.

text.p: Cambodian co-Premier Hun Sen on Monday warned that anyone who negotiated with the leaders of the collapsing Khmer Rouge movement were breaking the law and would face arrest.

Hun Sen said government officials should not hold talks with Khieu Samphan, president of the rebel movement's provisional government, or any other top leader and demanded senior Khmer Rouge rebels be arrested and brought to trial.

"Khieu Samphan has been supporting Pol Pot from the very beginning to the very end, so there is no way to stage any negotiations with Khieu Samphan, but now there have been negotiations with Khieu Samphan, which is an illegal issue," he said in speech broadcast on local radio.

His comments came after his partner in Cambodia's fragile coalition government, co-Premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh, told reporters he met Khieu Samphan three weeks ago near his rebel stronghold to talk peace.

Hun Sen said under Cambodian law, negotiating with the Khmer Rouge was illegal. Worse, he said, Khieu Samphan, a political ally of Ranariddh, had opposed him and therefore opposed the Cambodian government.
"While Khieu Samphan is cursing Hun Sen, there is no way for them to negotiate with Khieu Samphan," he said, without naming the negotiators. "I can arrest them if they try to break the law."
